purpose: Imiquimod is a cream applied to the skin to treat certain skin conditions caused by viruses or abnormal cell growth. It is commonly used for genital warts, certain pre-cancerous skin patches (actinic keratoses), and a type of superficial skin cancer called basal cell carcinoma. Your doctor has chosen this cream because it can help your body fight these conditions from the outside in.
how_it_works: Imiquimod works by waking up your own immune system right at the spot where you apply the cream. Think of it like sending a signal flare to your body's defense soldiers, telling them to come and attack the problem area. It does not kill the virus or abnormal cells directly — instead, it helps your own body do the fighting.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects happen right where you apply the cream. You may notice redness, itching, burning, flaking, or mild swelling of the skin — this is actually a sign the cream is working. Some people also experience small sores or crusting at the application site. These usually go away after treatment is finished.
warnings: Do not use more cream than prescribed or apply it more often than directed, as this can cause severe skin reactions. Keep the cream away from your eyes, mouth, and nostrils. Do not cover the treated area with tight bandages or wrappings unless your doctor tells you to. If you are pregnant or breastfeeding, talk to your doctor before using this medication. Sun sensitivity can increase, so protect the treated area from sunlight.
typical_dosing: Dosing depends on what condition is being treated. For genital warts, you typically apply the cream 3 nights per week at bedtime, wash it off after 6 to 10 hours, and continue for up to 16 weeks. For actinic keratoses, it is often applied 2 to 3 times per week for several weeks. Always follow your doctor or pharmacist's exact instructions, as dosing varies by condition and the specific product strength you are given.
